architecture: v3 (architecture 3, re-root at wave 1: which collections centre's overflow earns a sixth team, or none)
slot_note: re-root of the task128 slot in oviya1301's wave 1; the world comes from analytical_tasks/05_decision_support/DS04 (an arrears-outreach team and the days its list outruns it), moved from a utility to a bank's card collections; the seed's withheld rule and decoy are not used, and the pitfall is re-found from the data
niche: a Canadian regional bank's early-stage credit card collections: five regional collections centres call accounts on the first business day after they reach 30 days past due, and the bank decides which centre gets a sixth team for 2027, or none
stakeholder_role: director of collections operations at a Canadian regional bank, who decides which of the five regional collections centres gets a sixth early-stage team in 2027, or none

spine.entity: one account listed for an early-stage call on one business day, with its position in the centre's list that day

world.geography: Canada (Ontario and Manitoba; fictional bank, real cities for its centres)
world.org_type: regional bank with a credit card book of about 400,000 accounts and five regional collections centres

driver: A contact's effect is read only where the day's queue of units outran the team, comparing the units placed before the day's last contacted position with those placed after it on the same list, because units contacted at other times are the ones that respond and would have resolved anyway, units missing from the queue for other reasons could never be contacted, and the queue's order comes from a key unrelated to the outcome; read that way, no candidate clears the funding bar that every pooled or score-adjusted comparison clears.
driver_concrete: A collections call's effect on rolls to 90 days past due is measured only on the days a centre's 30-day dialler list outran its team, comparing accounts listed above the day's last attempted call with those below it on the same list, because accounts reached on other days are the customers who pay anyway, accounts off the dialler list (no valid phone, an arrangement already in place) could never be called, and the list is ordered by the card platform's partition key; on that comparison the best centre prevents about 2 rolls per 100 accounts called against the 3.4 the funding rule needs, so no centre gets the team.
stump: A competent solver compares accounts the centre's team called with accounts it did not, from the account register's 30-day arrears flag and adjusted for the behaviour score, and funds the centre whose called accounts roll least, at about 4 rolls prevented per 100 (figures fixed at design), because the uncalled include accounts with no valid phone and accounts listed on the big billing cycles' days, when the team never reaches the bottom of the list, both of which roll more for reasons a call does not change.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who cleans the call log, the dialler lists and the delinquency ledger and reads the funding rule right compares attempted with unattempted listed accounts by centre, adjusted for the behaviour score and pooled over the months, and funds a centre at about 4 rolls prevented per 100, because the unattempted accounts come from the large billing cycles' list days and roll more for reasons no score records; only the same-day comparison on over-capacity days measures the effect, and it falls short at every centre.
domain_test: Collections strategy is judged on incremental cures against a counterfactual, champion-challenger tests and the natural experiments capacity gives, which is collections analytics' own method for funding a team; with another field's nouns there is no delinquency roll, no dialler list and no capacity overflow, and the task stops reading the same.
layer1: a dialler list export per centre and day with list positions, re-listed accounts and test accounts
a call log at attempt grain (several attempts per account per day, dispositions in two code sets either side of a 2025 dialler upgrade)
a capacity log of each team's staffed seats and attempts per day, with a centre that merged two teams mid-2025
an account register with the nightly ageing job's arrears flag, which counts accounts the protocol keeps off the list
a monthly delinquency ledger with re-aged accounts, charge-offs and accounts sold to a debt buyer
the collections protocol and the credit policy's funding rule, filed once each

lineage.architecture: v1 (harden loop 0): whole-host rebuild valuation as the decisive rung, one colocated ticket spending the month's drains
lineage.fate: solved by the in-house plain solver in round 1 (2026-10-10); kept as the stop rung of loop 1
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is what one use of the binding resource removes, which is everything on the member that the current baseline fixes rather than the single item the request names, because each use rebuilds the member from that baseline; a ledger that credits each request with its own item reproduces every closed period, so per-item valuation spends the scarce uses on the members with the richest single item instead of the members carrying the most in total, and the constrained candidates need far fewer requests for far more removal than the per-item reading allows.

lineage.architecture: v2 (the ticket's reach: one change request per drain window)
lineage.fate: shipped 10-10 after solver round 2 missed (55.3) and a judge FIX_NOW; returned FAILED_TO_STUMP from the portal; spent at the wave-1 re-root 2026-10-12 (rule application as the decisive step; IT patch remediation has no client-domain task type serving Opportunity Sizing)
lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is how many requests it takes to spend a binding resource whose budget is stated for the whole period, because each request draws only on the capacity of the one interval it is booked into; a plan that values every use correctly but files one request against the period's whole budget reaches one interval's share, so the constrained candidates need one request per interval and the unconstrained candidates give up that many places under the cap.
